simple.meaning: מַדּוּעַ (maddûwaʻ) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “what (is) known? ; i.e. (by implication) (adverbially) why?.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 72 times across Genesis, Exodus, Leviticus, Numbers, Joshua, and 14 more, beginning at Genesis 26:27. Its contexts include family, kingship, Egypt, Israel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to מַדּוּעַ (H4069).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: מַדּוּעַ (maddûwaʻ) / H4069 is traced through Genesis 26:27, Genesis 40:7, Exodus 1:18, Exodus 2:18 as a generated source-based concept entry.

definitions.full: H4069. maddua מַדּוּעַ 61 and :( Exod 18:19 ) מַדֻּעַ adverb wherefore? (probably contracted from מַהיָּֿדוּעַ what being known ? i.e. from what motive? so Ges Ew §325 c Ol §223 f , compare in Greek τί μαθών ;) — wherefore? on what account ? Gen 26:27 אֵלָ֑י בָּאתֶם מַדּוּעַ , 40:7 ; Exod 1:18 ; 2:18 ; 3:8 (in an indirect question), 5:14 ; 18:14 ; Lev 10:17 ; Josh 17:14 (all in Hexateuch), Judg 5:28 (twice in verse); 2Sam 3:7 ; 11:10 etc., Isa 5:4 ; 50:2 ; 63:2 (all in Isaiah); in Jeremiah 16 t., oft, rhetorically, after a double question introduced by הֲאִ֗֗֗ם , expressing affected surprise: Jer 2:14 (see Gf) is Israel a slave (unable to defend himself)? wherefore , then, is he become a prey? (some other cause must therefore be found for Israel's misfortune), 2:31 ; 8:5 , 19 , 22 ; 14:19 ; 22:28 ; 49:1 , compare 30:6 ; Job 3:12 ; 18:8 (never in Psalms).
